r.정치 구도: Belgium is a constitutional monarchy in which real power lies with parliament and the prime minister. Flanders in the north speaks Dutch, Wallonia in the south speaks French, and together with bilingual Brussels the three regions have wide autonomy. There are practically no nationwide parties, so parties that ran in separate language areas have to build coalitions, and after the 2010 election forming a government took close to a year and a half. After the 2024 election the New Flemish Alliance, long an advocate of Flemish independence, took the prime minister's post for the first time, and a five-party coalition took office in February 2025. The coalition wants to cut pension and welfare spending to bring down a budget deficit above 5% of GDP, and unions have answered with a series of general strikes since 2025. When budget talks stalled in November 2026 the prime minister offered to resign, but the king did not accept.

t.why: Brussels hosts the European Commission, the Council of the EU and NATO headquarters, which makes it the stage for much of Europe's diplomatic news. The port of Antwerp-Bruges is one of Europe's largest. Euroclear, the securities settlement house in Brussels, holds most of the roughly 210 billion euros of Russian central bank assets frozen in the EU. When the EU proposed lending to Ukraine against that money, Belgium blocked it, saying it could not carry the risk of Russian lawsuits and retaliation on its own. In December 2025 the EU instead agreed to raise 90 billion euros through joint borrowing. Its colonial past in what are now the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and Burundi means it often weighs in on Central African affairs.
t.rel: The 'capital of Europe', home to the headquarters of the EU and NATO. Divided between Dutch- and French-speaking communities, it often takes a long time to form a government.
t.korea: Relations began with a treaty of amity and commerce with the Korean Empire in 1901, and 2026 marks 125 years of ties. About 3,500 Belgians served in the Korean War, and a battalion formed with troops from Luxembourg fought in the Battle of the Imjin River in April 1951. Belgium's defense minister at the time even left his post to serve in Korea himself. The Belgian company Umicore set up a plant in Cheonan in 1999 and became the first company in Korea to make cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries; Cheonan is still home to its largest battery materials research center and several plants. Trade between the two countries runs under the Korea-EU free trade agreement, provisionally applied since 2011.
t.know: In the village of Baarle-Hertog, the border with the Netherlands runs between houses, and the front door decides which country a house is in.
etext: Next to the port of Antwerp-Bruges is one of Europe's leading chemical clusters. Sitting between big markets like Germany, France and the Netherlands, it draws many logistics companies.
Belgium is a major exporter of medicines. Pfizer's plant in Puurs made COVID-19 vaccines for the world, and Janssen also started out in Belgium.
Companies that once ran colonial-era mines have reinvented themselves as makers of battery materials and recyclers of precious metals.
Labor costs and taxes are high, and government debt is larger than GDP. With powers split among the regions, even a single reform needs agreement from several governments.
